rule: IDs are never reused and run in version order. A CHANGED re-run is explained by Bk when recorded version < Bk.version <= this build's version, and the run's verb is in scope.verbs (or scope.verbs holds *), or one of its flags is in scope.options, or one of its input files has an extension in scope.inputFormats. An empty scope means the change has no command-line route (library or app only). Each entry claims its effect on the fields it moves: a bound (maxAbs and/or maxRel per value), an exact transform (new = factor x old, or a factor range), or a qualitative transition (from -> to, for a status or the exit code). A field outside its claim is EXCEEDS-CLAIM; claims of several IDs on one field add when all are bounds and are AMBIGUOUS otherwise; a field no claim covers is UNEXPLAINED. An entry with no claims explains nothing on its own.

scope.condition: an LCC or multi-terminal DC converter with a tap step below 1e-6 (any reader, refused by GridModel.Validate); a PSS/E J or K field of -2147483648; a RAWX cell with a line break or control character; a single CIM .xml over 256 MiB; a cgmes-study listing documents over 1 GiB in all; a COMTRADE sample number above 2147483647; a side file reached through a link to an ancestor of /dev, /proc or /sys; an rpc --listen request without the token (now checked before the id), or a connection that does not complete its first request within the deadline; a profiler switch set to a value the runtime reads as non-zero other than 1 (2, ff, 0x2, -1, 1x) with a profiler path set (exit 78 where it started); crossval on Linux or macOS, or with only relative PATH folders, where only a bare python or python3 was left (exit 77 where it started one)

entries.magnitude: no number changes for a valid case: the tap search takes the same steps as before for every real step. Such an input, which was read (or hung, or was an internal error), is refused with exit 1 naming it; such a connection is closed

entries.title: Correctness: IEC 60909 K_T c_max from the LV side, distance relays on a collapsed loop voltage, harmonic series-capacitor scaling, probabilistic probabilities over converged samples, QSTS devices at constant power, no tap steps on an open transformer, saturation points in either order, motor RK4 sub-steps

scope.condition: iec60909 --corrections with a transformer whose LV side is at or below 1 kV; a distance relay whose loop voltage collapses (a bolted fault at the relay point); a harmonic study with a line of negative X or a branch of negative B; a probabilistic AC load flow with samples that do not converge; a QSTS or hosting study with PV, storage or a load addition on a bus with a voltage-dependent load; an OLTC or flow control on an out-of-service transformer; an exciter record with E1 above E2; an induction motor load stepped beyond RK4's stability bound, 2.5 / (decay + 2 pi f |1 - w|) (a stalled slow motor above about 7.3 ms at 50 Hz or 6.1 ms at 60 Hz; a stalled fast motor such as the WECC CMLD motor A above about 4.7 ms at 60 Hz, so at the 5 ms default)

entries.magnitude: K_T x 1.05 / 1.10 (-4.5 %) on an LV-side transformer at or below 1 kV, maximum Ik'' at its LV board up to about +4.5 %; a collapsed distance loop is decided by its memory voltage (a bus fault behind the relay no longer trips zone 1); a series capacitor's harmonic impedance falls by h^2 at order h; violation probabilities rise by up to the failed share and such a run is INCOMPLETE (exit 3); PV, storage and load additions keep their set power (a 1 MW PV unit at 0.95 pu on a constant-impedance bus injected 0.9025 MW); every other case, h = 1, an ascending saturation pair and a step inside the RK4 bound (at the 5 ms default every motor with decay + 2 pi f |1 - w| at or below 500 1/s) are unchanged bit for bit
